newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy Secretary resigns effective Jan. 20.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy Secretary resigns effective Jan. 20.

text.p: U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary, who drew criticism for her costly overseas travels, has submitted a letter of resignation that President Bill Clinton will accept, the White House said on Wednesday.

"The president has, with great gratitude for her exemplary service at the Energy Department, indicated he would accept" O'Leary's resignation," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters at a briefing.
McCurry said Clinton did not ask for her resignation.
The Energy Department in a statement said O'Leary's resignation would be effective Jan. 20.
It said O'Leary met Clinton on Tuesday and submitted her resignation on Wednesday.
O'Leary said early in her four-year tenure at the department that she did not anticipate staying on for a second term.
She drew fire earlier this year for making extensive, and some critics said extravagant, trips to promote U.S. energy enterprises overseas.
"Under Secretary O'Leary's leadership, the Clinton administration has addressed critical national issues and made clear progress for the American people," the Energy Department's statement said.
